key_insight: The paper introduces "Sustainability Robotics" as a new field that unifies robotics research around sustainability goals. It proposes a shared framework to reduce fragmentation and increase both environmental and societal impact.
problem_solved: Robotics research is often fragmented across applications and lacks a common sustainability-oriented direction. The paper addresses the need for a discipline that connects robot design with solving sustainability challenges.
method: Defines Sustainability Robotics as a discipline with three guiding principles.
Introduces two dimensions: sustainable design and robotics for sustainability.
Frames robotics research around societal and environmental impact to guide future work.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clear lens for designing robotics systems that are not just technically effective, but also responsible and sustainability-centered. It can help align research agendas, evaluation criteria, and system design with real-world impact.
visual_elements: A two-axis framework showing sustainable design vs. robotics for sustainability.
An icon-based diagram for the three guiding principles.
A before/after graphic showing fragmented robotics research vs. unified Sustainability Robotics.
A flowchart linking robotics methods to environmental and societal outcomes.
paper_authors: S. Song, B. Mazzolai, M. Kovač
